packageRules.description: A PostgreSQL major bump in the ClusterImageCatalog must not be merged as-is: each entry is keyed by `major:`, so a new major is a new entry plus a Cluster change (CNPG offline pg_upgrade), not a tag bump. Keep the PR as a notification, but flag it. Minor bumps within the major stay automerged.
packageRules.commitMessageSuffix: (DO NOT MERGE - add a new major entry instead)
prBodyNotes:
> [!CAUTION]
> **Do not merge this PR.** It swaps the image under the existing (old) `major:` catalog entry for a new PostgreSQL major, which would put new-major binaries on old-major data.
>
> To upgrade instead:
> 1. Add a **new** `- major: N` entry to `apps/cnpg/pre-install/clusterimagecatalog.yaml` (keep the old one for rollback).
> 2. Check that the CNPG release in use lists the new major as supported.
> 3. In `apps/cnpg/post-install/postgresql-cluster.yaml`, bump `imageCatalogRef.major`. Optionally change the barman `serverName` (e.g. `postgres-pgN`) in the same commit to keep the old major's archive separate; keeping it is safe as long as the WAL timeline before the upgrade is not 1.
> 4. After the upgrade: run `update_extensions.sql` if `pg_upgrade` left one in `PGDATA`, `ANALYZE`, wait for a fresh base backup, update `resources/postgres-cloud-restore.yaml`.
> 5. Remove the **old** `major:` entry from the catalog. Renovate then auto-closes this PR.
>
> Do not close this PR by hand: its branch is named after the new major (`…-N.x`), the same branch the new entry's minor bumps will use. While the old entry exists, every N.x minor bump lands in this PR and inherits the `do-not-merge` label.

packageRules.description: Causes the bot to create a PR (and thus, an email notification), whenever there is a new Renovate version

customManagers.description: Update versions in Ansible vars with renovate comments

Update a version pinned in a shell variable inside an app values.yaml (e.g. transmission's initContainer that downloads the Flood web UI from a GitHub release), annotated with a renovate comment. The datasource is taken FROM the comment (github-releases, etc.).
